chunks: And Abu Ayyub narrated from Hariz from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the son of a violated woman, against whom a man fabricates an accusation and says to him, 'O son of an adulteress.'
He عليه السلام said: 'I hold that the legal punishment of eighty lashes is upon him, and he must repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for what he said.'

key_terms.الْمَغْصُوبَةِ: a woman who was violated or overpowered against her right
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes as the specified hadd penalty
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: the honorific description of Allah as Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.يَا ابْنَ الْفَاعِلَةِ: an insulting accusation impugning a person's lineage through zinā

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on falsely calling someone the son of an adulteress in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning false attribution of zinā through abusive speech directed at someone by insulting his lineage. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such slander incurs the hadd punishment of eighty lashes and requires tawbah to Allah عز وجل.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5086 - Abu Ayyub narrated from Hariz from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:
I asked Imam (as) about a man falsely accusing the son of a woman whose rights were violated (Al-maghsubah) by saying to him, "O' son of an adulteress."
Imam (as) said: "I believe he deserves the legal punishment of eighty lashes and must repent to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for what he has said."
